active_paradigms.idea: Incremental cost model: replace repeated full-sequence oracle calls with a fast internal makespan simulator enabling massive search speedup
active_paradigms.description: The current bottleneck is that every local move calls workload.get_opt_seq_cost on the full sequence (O(n) or worse per evaluation). Reverse-engineer or reimplement the makespan computation locally so that a swap/move can be evaluated incrementally: maintain per-transaction start/finish times and per-key last-access state, and when a transaction moves position, only recompute the affected suffix or use conflict-graph shortest-path reasoning (makespan of a serial schedule equals the critical path in the precedence DAG induced by the ordering). Precompute the conflict graph between transactions (which pairs conflict on which keys, and whether the conflict forces wait-for edges). Then a candidate ordering's cost is the longest path in a DAG, which can be computed in O(n + edges) — orders of magnitude faster than repeated oracle calls. This allows 100-1000x more local search iterations within the same 110s budget, dramatically deepening the 2-opt/or-opt/ILS search already present.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: makespan on all three workloads via much deeper local search and larger neighborhood exploration
active_paradigms.cautions: Must replicate the simulator's semantics exactly (verify against workload.get_opt_seq_cost on random sequences). Keep a fallback to the oracle call if unsure. Cache costs keyed by tuple(seq) to avoid recomputation.

active_paradigms.idea: Conflict-graph DAG construction: build precedence/critical-path model and order transactions by longest-path (Graham-style list scheduling) seeds
active_paradigms.description: Build a directed conflict multigraph where an edge t1->t2 exists if t1 and t2 conflict on a key and t1's conflicting operation comes first in t1's op sequence relative to t2's (or both directions if order-agnostic). Compute edge weights from operation positions to estimate forced delay. Then find a transaction ordering that minimizes the critical path: repeatedly select the next transaction using a priority rule based on the longest path to sink in the remaining graph (like Graham list scheduling / Hu's algorithm adapted to weighted DAGs), with tie-breaking by number of downstream conflicts. This gives a principled construction heuristic that directly targets makespan structure rather than blind greedy-by-cost. Use it to generate high-quality seeds, then hand off to the existing local search which will start from much better baselines.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: quality of initial schedules (better seeds mean local search converges to lower local optima)
active_paradigms.cautions: The DAG must be acyclic only if the ordering is consistent with it; use it as a heuristic guide, not a hard constraint. Validate final sequence with the real cost function.

active_paradigms.idea: Independent-component decomposition + exact DP on small components using networkx graph analysis
active_paradigms.description: Transactions that share no keys with any other transaction can be placed anywhere at zero conflict cost — identify them via key-transaction incidence and remove them from the combinatorial core, reinserting them greedily at the end. For the remaining core, detect connected components of the conflict graph; each component can be scheduled independently (no cross-conflicts), so run the expensive exact/heuristic search per component and concatenate. If a component is small (<= ~12 txns), solve it exactly via Held-Karp-style DP over bitmask orderings using the fast internal cost function. Use networkx (connected_components, dag_longest_path) to structure this decomposition. This converts one n=100 problem into several small near-exact problems.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: makespan by achieving exact optima on decomposed subproblems instead of heuristic solutions on the monolithic instance
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep the existing time budget management and final validation assert. Avoid spending too long on exact DP for n=100; use it only on detected small independent components.
